question: At a mass-casualty incident, a victim is breathing at 24 breaths per minute, has a radial pulse, and obeys commands. Which START triage colour should be assigned?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Red is assigned when respirations are >30/min OR there is no radial pulse OR the victim cannot obey commands. This victim meets none of those criteria.
Correct. Respirations 10–29/min + radial pulse present + obeys commands = Yellow (delayed). The victim is stable enough to wait once higher-priority casualties are treated.
Green is the 'walking wounded' — victims able to walk to a collection point. This victim's respiratory rate of 24/min and possible inability to walk make Yellow the appropriate category.
Black is assigned to victims who are not breathing after airway repositioning, or to expectant casualties with unsurvivable injuries when resources are overwhelmed.

overallFeedback.feedback: In START triage, check respirations first (>30 = Red), then radial pulse (absent = Red), then ability to obey commands (cannot = Red). If all three are within limits, assign Yellow.
Correct. START triage: respirations, radial pulse, and ability to obey commands — all within normal limits here — assign Yellow (delayed).
